description: Build the frontend battle-enhancement UX and wire difficulty+seed end to end, with JA/EN parity and prefers-reduced-motion respected. Adds: a difficulty selector (弱い/普通/強い), an enemy PREVIEW generated client-side via the SAME shared generateEnemy (name/sprite/stats + difficulty) BEFORE committing to the fight so preview==actual fight, a low-HP warning/confirm before fighting, the win/loss/draw + streak record shown in StatsPanel, and new pure ui-helpers with unit tests. Depends on FEAT-002 and FEAT-003.
steps: api.ts: change `battle(monsterId: string)` to `battle(monsterId: string, difficulty: Difficulty, seed: number)` and include difficulty+seed in the POST JSON body `{ monsterId, difficulty, seed }`. Import Difficulty from @ddm/shared. Keep BattleApiResult shape.

useMonster.ts: (a) In advance(), also normalize the record for legacy saves by composing normalizeBattleRecord with the existing normalizeAffection(applyTimePassage(...)) so live state always has a numeric record for the UI. (b) Change battle() to accept (difficulty: Difficulty, seed: number) and pass them to api.battle; keep the optimistic commit/setLastBattle/setBattleLog flow. (c) Expose the chosen seed handling: the hook does not need to own the seed; the BattlePanel will pick difficulty+seed and pass them into game.battle. Update the UseMonsterState.battle signature + the returned callback accordingly.

App.tsx: update the BattlePanel usage to pass the new props. The player's live monster (game.monster) provides stageId/stats for the preview; pass game.battle (now taking difficulty+seed) down. Keep playerStartHp recovery via playerStartHpFromLog unchanged.

ui-helpers.ts (pure, unit-tested in game-ui.test.ts): add (a) `difficultyLabel(difficulty: Difficulty, lang: Lang): string` sourced from new i18n keys (弱い/普通/強い ; Easy/Normal/Hard); (b) `DIFFICULTIES: Difficulty[]` ordering ['easy','normal','hard'] for rendering the selector; (c) `pickBattleSeed(): number` a thin wrapper returning a fresh random 32-bit seed (Math.floor(Math.random()*0xffffffff)) — keep the RANDOMNESS out of the render path so tests stay deterministic by not testing the random value itself, only that it returns a finite integer in range; (d) `battleRecordSummary(record: BattleRecord, lang: Lang)` -> a localized string like `3勝 1敗 0分 / 連勝2` (JA) and `3W 1L 0D / Streak 2` (EN), sourced from i18n templates; (e) `isLowHp(hp: number, maxHp: number): boolean` returning true when hpPercent(hp,maxHp) < a documented LOW_HP_BATTLE_PERCENT threshold (e.g. 30, reuse/define a local const; document it). Use the shared battleRecordOf when reading the record so legacy state is safe.

BattlePanel.tsx: add new props for difficulty state + preview + record. Concretely: (1) Local state for selected difficulty (default 'normal') and a current seed (initialized via pickBattleSeed, regenerated when difficulty changes OR after a fight so each preview/fight pair gets a fresh seed). (2) Compute the preview enemy on the client with the SHARED generateEnemy(playerStageId, difficulty, seed) so preview===the enemy the backend will regenerate from the same inputs. Render a preview block: enemy localized display name (difficulty prefix + stage label via i18n, NOT the raw Monster.name), the MonsterSprite for playerStageId (reuses stage sprite), and the enemy stats (maxHp/atk/def), plus the selected difficulty. (3) Replace the hardcoded enemyMaxHp (stage*0.9) and enemyName reconstruction used by the #9 animation with the PREVIEWED enemy's maxHp and localized name, so the animation matches the real fight. (4) A difficulty selector (radio group or buttons) with role=radiogroup / aria-pressed, keyboard accessible, labeled via i18n; selecting a difficulty updates the preview live. (5) The fight button: when the player's current HP is low (ui-helpers isLowHp on playerStartHp or the live monster hp), show a warning before fighting. Reuse the accessible confirm pattern from App.tsx reset dialog (role=alertdialog, aria-modal, focus moved to confirm, Escape cancels, focus restored) OR an inline warning with an explicit confirm button; if low-HP, the primary button first surfaces the warning and only the confirm actually calls onBattle. If HP is not low, fight immediately. (6) onBattle must now pass the SELECTED difficulty and the CURRENT seed up to game.battle(difficulty, seed); after a fight, regenerate the seed for the next preview. (7) Respect prefers-reduced-motion: any new transitions/animations for the preview must be disabled under the existing reduced-motion CSS approach; reuse existing CSS conventions, no new blocking animation.

StatsPanel.tsx: render the win/loss/draw + current streak using battleRecordSummary(battleRecordOf(monster), lang) in an accessible row (aria-label combining the label and the summary, mirroring the affection/fullness rows which are not color-only). Add a new i18n label key e.g. stats.record.

i18n.ts: add BOTH ja and en for every new key. Required new keys (names illustrative, keep consistent): difficulty.easy (弱い/Easy), difficulty.normal (普通/Normal), difficulty.hard (強い/Hard), difficulty.label (難易度/Difficulty), battle.preview (このモンスターと戦う？ or 相手プレビュー / Enemy preview), battle.enemyNameWithDifficulty template e.g. `{difficulty} 野生の{label}モンスター` JA and `{difficulty} Wild {label} Monster` EN (used for the localized enemy display name combining difficulty + stage label), battle.lowHpWarning (HPが低い状態です。このまま挑戦しますか？ / HP is low. Fight anyway?), battle.lowHpConfirm (挑戦する / Fight), battle.lowHpCancel (やめる / Cancel), stats.record (戦績 / Record), and the battleRecordSummary template pieces (e.g. stats.recordSummary `{w}勝 {l}敗 {d}分 / 連勝{s}` JA and `{w}W {l}L {d}D / Streak {s}` EN). Reuse existing keys where possible (e.g. status.busy). Keep JA output byte-identical for all PRE-EXISTING keys. Do NOT remove battle.enemyName if still referenced; otherwise update references.

game-ui.test.ts: add unit tests (node:test + assert/strict, existing style) for the new pure helpers: difficultyLabel for every difficulty in ja AND en; DIFFICULTIES ordering; battleRecordSummary formatting for a sample record in ja AND en (asserting exact strings) and that it reads a legacy (undefined-record) monster safely via battleRecordOf; isLowHp boundary behavior (just below vs at/above the threshold, and the maxHp<=0 guard); pickBattleSeed returns a finite integer within [0, 0xffffffff]. Do NOT assert the random value itself.
Run both test suites and the build. Fix any JA parity / type errors (EN dict is a typed Record<MessageKey,string> so a missing EN key is a compile error).
acceptance_criteria: api.battle sends {monsterId, difficulty, seed}; useMonster.battle(difficulty, seed) threads them through; App wires BattlePanel accordingly.

BattlePanel shows a difficulty selector (弱い/普通/強い) and an enemy preview (localized name + stage sprite + stats + difficulty) generated via the SHARED generateEnemy with the client-chosen seed, so the preview equals the enemy the backend regenerates; the #9 animation uses the previewed enemy's name/maxHp (no stage*0.9 reconstruction).
A low-HP warning/confirm appears before fighting when the player's HP is low, is keyboard accessible, and respects prefers-reduced-motion; fighting proceeds immediately when HP is not low.
StatsPanel displays wins/losses/draws + current streak in an accessible (not color-only) row, reading the record via battleRecordOf so legacy state is safe.
Every new i18n string has BOTH ja and en; all pre-existing JA strings are byte-identical.
New ui-helper unit tests pass; frontend test count rises above 79 and `npm run test -w @ddm/frontend` is green; `npm test` (shared) stays green; `npm run build` succeeds.
findings: Implemented end to end. Verification: `npm run test -w @ddm/frontend` 88 pass (baseline 79); `npm test` (shared) 94 pass (green); `npm run build` succeeds across shared/backend/frontend/infra (JA/EN parity enforced at compile). Notes: (1) BattlePanel now computes the preview enemy via shared generateEnemy(playerStageId, difficulty, seed) and feeds enemy.stats.maxHp + the localized battle.enemyNameWithDifficulty name into the #9 animation, replacing the stage*0.9 reconstruction; the simulateBattle log format and ui-helpers parse/battleLogLine were left untouched. (2) App.tsx needed NO change for the battle signature: it already passes onBattle={game.battle} plus player stage/stats and playerStartHp via playerStartHpFromLog, and the hook's battle(difficulty, seed) is assignable to the panel's (difficulty, seed)=>void prop. (3) Low-HP warning is an inline role=alertdialog confirm reusing the reset-dialog a11y pattern (focus to confirm, two-button Tab trap, Escape cancels, focus restored). (4) Difficulty selector is a role=radiogroup of role=radio buttons with aria-checked, keyboard reachable. (5) New i18n keys added with BOTH ja+en: difficulty.label/easy/normal/hard, battle.preview, battle.enemyNameWithDifficulty, battle.lowHpWarning/lowHpConfirm/lowHpCancel, stats.record, stats.recordSummary. No pre-existing JA strings changed (git diff shows additions only). (6) New reduced-motion CSS block disables the cosmetic difficulty-btn transition. Tooling note: the grep_search/file content-search tool returned no matches inside packages/frontend (likely ignore-filtering); used read_file + bash grep instead for that subtree. --- REVIEW FIX PASS (2026-10-05-074421-review.md, NEEDS_CHANGES): Addressed the blocking finding that the #9 replay scaled the enemy HP bar against the WRONG enemy. Root cause: fightNow() called setSeed(pickBattleSeed()) synchronously right after onBattle(), recomputing the memoized preview enemy (keyed on seed) to the NEXT enemy before the async fought result/log landed and animated. Chose approach (b) SNAPSHOT: at dispatch time fightNow() now stores the fought enemy's {difficulty, maxHp} into new `foughtEnemy` state; the replay resolves its enemy via a new pure helper resolveAnimationEnemy(preview, fought) which prefers the fought snapshot over the live (reseeded) preview, falling back to the preview before any fight. The enemy NAME is re-derived in render from the snapshot's difficulty+stage (not baked in) so a mid-replay JA/EN language toggle still relocalizes, matching pre-fix behavior. The preview block now renders previewName/live enemy.stats (the next/fresh foe) while the replay animates the fought foe, resolving review issue #2 (preview no longer appears to swap the animating enemy's identity). Seed still regenerates after dispatch, so pressing fight again faces a fresh enemy as intended; backend fight/reward/record unchanged (always used the original seed). TEST GAP addressed: added resolveAnimationEnemy to ui-helpers.ts (pure) and two node:test cases in game-ui.test.ts — the 'prefers the fought snapshot over a reseeded preview' case FAILS under the old reseed-before-animate behavior (asserts maxHp/name come from the fought enemy, not the reseeded preview). Verification after fix: `npm run test -w @ddm/frontend` 90 pass (was 88); `npm test` 94 pass; `npm run build` succeeds across all packages. No i18n keys added/changed; no new runtime deps. Status remains completed.
